interest: This docket sheet offers a valuable snapshot of late-prewar friction between the Japanese government and American officials over taxation and diplomatic prerogatives in 1940 and 1941. It illustrates Japanese administrative crackdowns on the perceived abuse of diplomatic privileges regarding automobile resales by foreign service personnel, as well as wartime/pre-war municipal revenue efforts in Kobe targeting foreign consular staff and American shipping firms such as the States Steamship Company with the local 'Citizens' Tax'.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46, dated October 12, 1945) cataloguing communications filed under decimal file 894.512 concerning taxation in Japan between March 1940 and January 1941. The indexed records (sub-numbers 54 to 56) address Japanese tax policies impacting American official personnel and commercial interests. Specifically, the entries cover a report from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on Japan's decision to levy sales taxes on automobiles owned by Foreign Service officers following alleged abuses of diplomatic privileges, as well as despatches from Consul Samuel Sokobin in Kobe regarding the erroneous assessment of the local 'Citizens' Tax' on American consular officers and an inquiry into the tax liability of American commercial maritime carriers, notably the States Steamship Company.

subfiles.about: A Department of State docket sheet indexing documents filed under decimal file 894.512 concerning taxation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46), compiled on October 12, 1945, records three documents from 1940 and 1941 relating to taxation in Japan under classification 894.512. It notes a March 1940 report from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding the Japanese government's decision to impose sales tax on automobiles belonging to Foreign Service officers due to alleged abuses of diplomatic privileges. It further indexes two January 1941 despatches from Consul Samuel Sokobin in Kobe concerning the exemption of consular and other American officials from the municipal 'Citizens' Tax' after an erroneous assessment, as well as an inquiry regarding the tax liabilities of American shipping enterprises including the States Steamship Company.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Taxation in Japan
